Hi Dara — great to connect this morning, thanks for the demo and the clear overview of FinThrive's EU customer use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps so our legal team can slot this: 

Summary from call:
- FinThrive will send Redwood personal data originating from EU residents for transaction enrichment and model inference (primary dataset contains healthcare claims metadata).
- You indicated FinThrive is the Data Controller for the record-level data; Redwood would operate as Processing vendor for the inference feature during pilot and production.
- HIPAA/PHI: you confirmed pilot will include PHI and you require a signed BAA for any PHI processing.
- SOC 2: you asked for our SOC 2 posture and an up-to-date report for procurement review.

Immediate asks for you to confirm (so legal can prepare the right paperwork):
1) Confirm that FinThrive expects Redwood to be the Processor (not joint-controller) across the integration.
2) Confirm preferred SCC module flavor for EU→US transfers (if you have a procurement preference).
3) Confirm that a BAA is required for pilot and whether it must be in place before any PHI is transmitted.

What we'll do next:
- I'll loop in Legal (Marissa + Laura) to draft a DPA + BAA combo and provide SCC module options.
- We'll attach our SOC 2 summary and the DPA draft for your review.
- Suggest a short legal-to-legal call early next week to finalize module selection and sign-off.

Would appreciate confirmations on the three bullets above; I'll mark this as high priority on our side.

Thanks,

Jordan — thanks for the heads-up and the call notes. Below is an initial compliance-first recommendation and an action list we can hand to procurement/legal at FinThrive.

Legal recommendation (short):
- Roles: Redwood will sign as Processor. We will not accept joint-controller language for this integration given our product architecture (we only perform inference and return transformed outputs).
- DPA: Draft a Processor DPA (standard clauses + Redwood processor annex). Include security controls summary and an audit cooperation clause.
- BAA: Draft a standalone BAA to be appended for PHI processing during pilot and for production where PHI is in-scope. Note: BAA obligations will be limited to the processing activities described in the DPA; tie definitions to the HIPAA terms FinThrive expects.
- SCCs: For EU→US transfers, propose the Controller-to-Processor SCC set (EU Commission 2021 module: Controller→Processor). We'll provide redlined SCC text so procurement can accept without further delay. If FinThrive insists on controller-to-controller, advise Procurement this will require additional legal review and may increase signing time.

Operational notes for Procurement/InfoSec: 
- SOC 2: Redwood's latest SOC 2 Type II (reporting period Jan–Dec 2026) is attached as a summary. Full report available under NDA; provide link or let me know if procurement needs the complete report.
- Security controls: include our encryption-in-transit and at-rest bullets, incident notification SLA (72 hours), and subprocessor list upon request.

Proposed attachments I will send now:
- dpa_draft_finthrive_v1.docx (Processor DPA draft with PHI/BAA annex)
- scc_options_summary.pdf (short matrix: Controller→Processor module recommended + short rationale)
- soc2_redwood_2026_summary.pdf (Executive summary of our SOC 2 Type II)

Next steps / timeline:
1) I will send the DPA + SCC redlines and the BAA draft to Dara & privacy@finthrive.com by end of day 11/16.
2) Proposed legal-to-legal call: Tue 11/16 11:00 AM ET (please confirm; Jordan to set invite).
3) If FinThrive confirms Controller→Processor SCCs and signs BAA, target full execution within 5 business days.

If procurement requests alternate SCC modules, we'll triage but expect extra review time.

Marissa Cole
